title: Bassoon
summary: No render yet. No complete bassoon air column is published in open sources: only ten tone holes of one German bassoon and nine of a different French one, a straight test bocal and a few global dimensions. A hunt of 11-08 found no table of the bore or the tone holes of a named modern bassoon. The one modern-bassoon database in preparation (Houde-Turcotte, ISMA 2019; Universite de Montreal, ITEMM and LAUM) is described in a methods paper that prints no bore or tone-hole data and no data statement, its tools having been tested on one instrument. A thesis reports bore and tone-hole dimensions of 36 baroque bassoons (Dart 2011, London Metropolitan University; read as a catalogue entry, not opened) and datasets exist for small-sized bassoons (the fagottini of the Fachhochschule Nordwestschweiz, on Zenodo), which are other instruments. No paper of the Detmold, Marseille or Bordeaux studies named in the blocked line was found, and the repository cites none. The instrument of the Iowa recordings, the comparison target, is not identified here as German or French system: its system is not known. The tables of the database would have to come from its author
physics_present: generic fs-duct conical and cylindrical segments, tone-hole side branches and a flanged bell load, the lumped single-reed owner and the physical baffled outlet receiver already run for the clarinet; none has been given this instrument's geometry
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two professional bassoon players are retained as player data
physics_missing: bore profile of the bocal, wing, boot, long joint and bell
positions and sizes of most tone holes, pads and key rise, and a fingering chart
a double-reed valve driving this bore
a single specimen: the two partial hole tables belong to different instruments and must not be merged
blocked: No complete published bassoon geometry; needs the measured bore and hole tables from the authors of the Detmold, Marseille or Bordeaux bassoon studies, or an owner measurement.
